title: Distinguish Observable Symptoms vs Assumptions
statement: Distinguish directly observable browser behavior from unverified assumptions in a failing user interface.

title: Form Falsifiable Debugging Hypotheses
statement: Form a falsifiable hypothesis regarding interface failure prior to inspecting source code or system internals.

title: Repair Disconnected Event Listeners
statement: Identify unattached event listeners and apply a targeted fix connecting the DOM trigger to the handler function.

title: Reconstruct Frontend Causal Chains
statement: Explain frontend runtime execution as an unbroken causal chain from user input through event dispatch, state mutation, and browser paint.

title: Inspect DOM Tree Structure and Attributes
statement: Use browser inspection tools to examine DOM node hierarchy, parent-child nesting, and element attributes.

title: Trace Event Propagation Flow
statement: Trace the lifecycle of a browser event across capture, target, and bubbling phases to determine handler execution order.

title: Predict Box Model Sizing and Overflow
statement: Calculate total element dimensions accounting for content, padding, border, and margin, and predict when overflow will trigger scrollbars or clipping.

title: Diagnose Selector Specificity Overrides
statement: Calculate selector specificity weight (inline, ID, class/attribute, type) and determine which CSS declaration takes precedence in conflicting cascades.

title: Isolate Grid and Flexbox Misalignment
statement: Diagnose why a multi-element layout collapsed or broke alignment by inspecting flex containers, grid template tracks, and intrinsic item sizing.

title: Model the HTML Document as a Tree
statement: Model an HTML document as a hierarchical tree of nested parent-child elements, where nesting is structural rather than cosmetic.

title: Configure Elements with Attributes
statement: Configure an HTML element's behavior using attributes, and distinguish the element itself from its configuration.

title: Structure a Document with Headings
statement: Use heading elements to construct a meaningful, hierarchical document outline based on structure rather than visual appearance.

title: Reference External Resources with Attributes
statement: Explain how an attribute like href or src names a separate resource for the browser to retrieve, distinct from the visible text or image that activates it.

title: Distinguish Sequential from Tabular Data
statement: Distinguish genuinely sequential information from tabular, two-dimensional relationships, and model each with the HTML structure that actually matches it.

title: Programmatically Associate Form Labels
statement: Construct a form control with a label that is programmatically associated to it, and explain why adjacency alone is not the same as association.
Apply core principles of The Web as a System

By the end of this module, the learner can trace a page from user action to rendered result, explain the browser/server boundary, distinguish HTML/CSS/JavaScript responsibilities, and identify the earliest changed boundary when something breaks.
Apply core principles of Thinking Like a Programmer

By the end of this module, the learner can turn a vague task into explicit steps, predict a sequence before execution, compare expected and actual behavior, locate the first meaningful mismatch, and make a small justified repair.
Apply core principles of HTML: Structure and Meaning

By the end of this module, the learner can build a valid, meaningfully structured HTML page, choose elements based on content purpose, use basic attributes, and organize page regions, lists, links, images, and forms without relying on visual styling.
Apply core principles of CSS: Make the Structure Visible

By the end of this module, the learner can style existing HTML deliberately, explain what each CSS rule is doing, predict simple cascade and box-model outcomes, style basic states, and investigate a visual problem without changing unrelated code.
Apply core principles of Layout and Responsive Design

By the end of this module, the learner can explain normal document flow, choose between ordinary flow, Flexbox, and Grid for a layout problem, control spacing and alignment deliberately, and adapt a layout to narrower screens without relying on random pixel nudges.
Apply core principles of Accessible Interface Craft

By the end of this module, the learner can treat accessibility as part of interface quality, choose meaningful HTML elements, build understandable headings and controls, provide useful text alternatives, label and explain form inputs, preserve keyboard access and visible focus, and review a page for common accessibility barriers.
Apply core principles of JavaScript: The Language of Behavior

By the end of this module, the learner can read JavaScript as a sequence of values and transformations, predict outcomes, write small functions, work with arrays and objects, trace decisions and loops, and repair a small program without guessing.
Apply core principles of JavaScript in the Browser

By the end of this module, the learner can inspect and change the current page, respond to browser events, read form input, control default browser actions, and preserve a small client-side preference between refreshes.
Apply core principles of TypeScript: Make Intent Explicit

By the end of this module, the learner can use TypeScript to make the intended shape of values explicit, let inference do useful work, type functions and object data, represent alternatives with unions, narrow safely before using a value, and write simple generic helpers that preserve relationships between input and output.
Apply core principles of Web Data and APIs

By the end of this module, the learner can explain an API as a communication contract, read a simple HTTP exchange, understand JSON as data, request data with `fetch`, reason about asynchronous results, represent loading/success/failure states, and investigate common browser-side request failures.
Apply core principles of Git, GitHub, and Team Workflow

By the end of this module, the learner can use Git as a safety and collaboration system: make focused commits, inspect changes, work on branches, synchronize with a remote repository, open a pull request, handle a simple merge conflict, and recover from common mistakes without panicking.
Apply core principles of React: Think in UI State

By the end of this module, the learner can design a small React interface around components, props, state, derived data, and explicit one-way data flow. They can identify the minimal state, decide where state should live, and repair UI logic without manually fighting the rendered output.
Apply core principles of React: Interaction and Effects

By the end of this module, the learner can build React interfaces that respond to user interaction, control form inputs with state, distinguish rendering from event logic and Effects, and use `useEffect` only when a component must synchronize with something outside React. They can choose the right dependency list, clean up synchronization work, and explain why an Effect should exist before writing one.
Apply core principles of React: Component Design and Application Patterns

By the end of this module, you can design React components with clear boundaries, treat props as deliberate component APIs, use composition instead of rigid component coupling, reason about data flow, choose sensible state ownership, avoid premature abstraction, and refactor an overgrown component without breaking the UI contract.
Apply core principles of Routing, Data Flow, and React Applications

By the end of this module, you can reason about a React application as a connected set of routes and state boundaries, use the URL as meaningful application state, compose nested screens, share state deliberately, choose between props, context, and reducers, and place data loading or mutations at a sensible application boundary.
Apply core principles of Next.js Application Engineering

By the end of this module, the learner can structure a Next.js App Router application, design route and layout boundaries, distinguish Server and Client Components, design loading/error experiences, use Route Handlers appropriately, perform server-side mutations, reason about environment-variable exposure, and make informed caching/revalidation decisions.
Apply core principles of Application State

By the end of this module, the learner can classify application state, choose a clear owner, avoid duplicate and contradictory state, use Context deliberately, distinguish server data from local drafts and persisted browser state, and design synchronization boundaries before choosing a state-management tool.
